public.defaultBody: Scan to enable multisig on this wallet. Your address stays the same; control becomes shared.
guideLines: Multisig adds shared control to your existing wallet. The receive address does not change.
Members put open codes on their own scenarios. Customers scan, then the wallet opens /o/… to sign.
TokenPocket / OKX / Bitget: scan from the wallet home screen. TronLink: open the link in Discover / Browser.
The open code expires. Tap “Refresh code” when it does.
public.homeLead: TRON (TRC20) multisig activation station. Members create their own multisig open codes and place them on apps that need it. After a customer scans, the wallet address stays the same; control becomes shared.
homePoints: After sign-in, set your two co-signer addresses. Your entry /p/u/{code} shows an open QR on the spot.
Under Scenarios, make a card (with ref) for each app and put the QR on a counter, H5, or campaign page.
Customers scan the scenario or entry QR; the wallet opens /o/{session} to sign.
The site default door is /open (staff addresses), separate from member entries. The intro home has no QR.

help.title: Help
help.subtitle: Crypto Wallet Streamline Multisig Station: members make open codes and place them on scenarios.
help.versionMismatch: Help version does not match the running app. Update under System Updates or contact support.

login.title: 0. Sign in
steps: Intro home top-right Sign in goes to /login. Staff and members use one form; you land in the matching panel. /branch/login still works.
Members: set Multisig Addresses, then make QRs under Scenarios. If a registration code is required, buy one or ask the site owner first. Customers scan /p/u/{code}; the wallet signs on /o/{session}.
About 5 failed attempts from the same account or IP locks login for ~15 minutes.
tips: Change the default admin password immediately after go-live.

password.title: 0.2 Change password
steps: After sign-in, open Password, verify the current password, then set a new one.

open.title: 1. Open codes and signing
steps: Members give customers a scenario card or private entry /p/u/{code}. That page shows an open QR in place (no redirect).
The wallet opens the sign page /o/{session}. After signing, the address stays the same; control becomes shared.
The site default door is /open (same page as decorated /p/…). It uses staff addresses, separate from member entries.
Open codes expire — refresh the QR page for a new one.
tips: Configure multisig addresses and enable wallet entries first.
Open codes are plain HTTPS. TokenPocket / OKX / Bitget: home scan works; TronLink: use Discover/Browser, not home scan.

network.title: 2. Network
steps: Super admin opens Network, picks Shasta or TRON mainnet, and saves.
Takes effect immediately; open-page QR and new sessions use the new network.
Mainnet and Shasta have separate multisig addresses — verify both after switching.
tips: Use mainnet in production; Shasta for testing.

presets.title: 3. Multisig addresses
steps: Open Multisig Addresses and configure exactly two co-signers for the current network.
Check Network first, then save addresses for that network.

wallets.title: 4. Opened
steps: View successfully opened 2/3-tier addresses (read-only).
Higher-tier opens are not shown here.

decor.title: 5. Public page design
steps: This is the open-page look: title, body, footer, images. Saves apply to /open immediately. It is not a scenario card.
Copy the stable /open URL for posters; custom /p/path is the same open page.
tips: Codes pasted into apps belong under Scenarios. Design only changes what customers see on the open page.

scenarios.title: 5.2 Scenarios
steps: These are cards you paste into an app or counter — not the open-page design. Members make a card per app and show the QR (/p/u/{code}).
Open-page look is under Public Page Design. Staff can also add cards (max 20, via /open).
The built-in counter card is admin-only. Members may create up to 5 cards each; they cannot see each other.
When the HQ renewal is limited, cards and QR codes stay visible; create and save are locked.
tips: Member scenario cards use /p/u/{code} plus a ref. Staff posters use fixed /open plus a ref.

members.title: 5.3 Member registration and billing
steps: Members controls public registration, codes, and USDT that members pay this site. Sidebar Renew with HQ is the owner paying HQ — different address and orders.
Three registration modes; you must click Save registration: off; open (no expiry, testing); code required (default 7 days).
If a code is required: generate codes, or enable on-chain purchase. Save this site’s TRON USDT address first, then enable. Visitors buy at /member/buy-register.
Defaults: code 10 USDT / 7 days, member plan 30 USDT / 30 days. After expiry, the member cannot sign in or open /p/u/{code}. Admins can extend +7 / +30 days.
Members set Multisig Addresses then make QRs under Scenarios. /p/u/{code} uses that member’s two addresses. Admins cannot edit member addresses.
tips: Site /open uses staff addresses; /p/u/{code} uses the member’s. Two fees: HQ renewal pays HQ; member plan pays this site’s address.

member-plan.title: 5.4 Member plan
steps: Member plan in the member panel only extends your member access. Send the exact USDT amount on TRON mainnet.
Do not pay Renew with HQ in the staff menu. That is the owner paying HQ.
Without a registration code, open /member/buy-register (the owner must have enabled purchase and set an address).
tips: After expiry you cannot sign in or issue codes from /p/u/{code} until you renew or an admin extends you.

license.title: 5.5 Renew with HQ
steps: Sidebar Renew with HQ: the owner renews this site's license with HQ. Pay the HQ address on the order. Not the same as member plan — members pay you; this page is you paying HQ.
The address for member codes / member plans is set under Members. Do not mix it with the HQ order.
tips: An expired HQ renewal limits public open and write actions. An expired member only affects that member.

open-wallets.title: 6. Wallet entries
steps: Enable wallet buttons customers can use. Wallets that scan more reliably are listed first.
QR codes stay HTTPS; enabling a wallet does not change the QR to a deep link.
If none are enabled, signing works only when a wallet is already injected.

update.title: 7. System updates
steps: Updates → Check for updates → Update now.
Updates preserve .env and the database.
Release notes show a short summary only (bug fixes / feature updates).
